brief.text: You've just joined **Pawprint Pantry** as its first in-house performance marketer. Pawprint Pantry is a D2C pet food brand selling fresh-cooked dog food online. The founder runs the business day to day, and an agency, Growthline Media, runs paid media.

brief.caption: Last month, as reported by each ad platform

brief.text: Same month, from the store backend

items: Average order value: **₹899**
Gross margin after product, shipping and payment costs: **45%**
About 31% of customers order again within 90 days.

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: It's your first morning at Pawprint Pantry. Looking at last month's numbers, **what worries you most, and what is the first number you would check before changing anything?**
Refer to specific figures. One sharp point beats a list of ten.

views.title: The budget cut

choices.label: Spread the cut evenly across channels

prompt.text: The founder has cut next month's paid media budget by **25%**, to **₹16,50,000**, and wants orders to stay roughly flat. Retargeting is small; leave it out of this decision.
**Where does most of the cut come from?** Pick one, then explain:

items: why this channel,
what you expect to happen to store orders next month (give a number and how you got it),
the risk you are accepting, and the early warning you would watch.

lookingFor: Commits and reasons from unit economics

prompt.text: Two weeks in, every channel is down roughly in proportion and store orders are down 35%, worse than the 25% cut would suggest.
The founder says: **"You didn't make a decision, you made a spreadsheet."** What do you change now?

Two weeks in, Meta-reported orders are down 40%, roughly as you planned. But Google Search orders are also down 15%, mostly on searches for "Pawprint Pantry", and your retargeting audiences have shrunk by about a third.
The founder asks: **"Was cutting Meta a mistake?"** What do you tell them, and what do you do this week?
Two weeks in, a competitor has started bidding on "Pawprint Pantry" as a keyword. Your brand CPC is up 60% and the competitor now appears above you for your own name on 54% of searches.
You cut Search. **What do you do this week, and what do you tell the founder?**

Two weeks in, a creator you paid last month posts about Pawprint Pantry without being paid. Over three days you get about 109 extra orders, almost all tagged "Direct / none" in analytics, and nobody uses a discount code.
The founder says: **"Influencers work when we don't pay them. Cancel all the contracts."** What do you tell them?
